In this Revecore conversation, Angela Troccoli sits down with Firoze Lafeer, who leads data science at Revecore, to break down what an AI agent actually is and what hospital leaders need to think about when building an AI strategy.
This discussion covers the practical difference between a chat-based AI tool and an agentic system that monitors, detects patterns, and acts on its own, why that distinction matters operationally, and what foundational steps organizations should take before investing in AI internally.
Key takeaways from the discussion:

An agent is an AI system with agency, meaning it takes action rather than only answering questions
The real difference between chat-based AI and agentic AI is autonomous or semi-autonomous pattern detection and action, without being explicitly prompted
Agentic capabilities are becoming standard across vendors and technologies, not a niche feature limited to one use case
Successfully launching an AI strategy starts with understanding what the technology is and isn't, and getting the right guidance

videos.title: Agent Q-Mix: RL for Multi-Agent LLM Topology
videos.description:
Agent Q-Mix learns who-talks-to-whom among LLM agents — using value-factorized
multi-agent RL to pick the right communication topology each round.

Each agent runs a shared network (a topology-aware GNN over the communication graph +
GRU memory + an MLP over 6 communication actions: work-alone, broadcast, query,
aggregate, handoff, debate). Per-agent Q-values merge into one team Q via the QMIX
mixing network, whose nonnegative weights guarantee monotonicity — so decentralized
greedy equals the centralized optimum.

In this video:
- The problem: choosing LLM communication topology
- Per-agent network: GNN + GRU + 6-action head
- QMIX mixing + the nonnegativity constraint
- IGM: why monotonicity makes greedy optimal
- CTDE + reward vs token cost
